links.comparator_used: ADAPT-CEC AI adjudication of all suspected events alone (and direct GPT 4o adjudication)
links.outcome: Accuracy of end point classification versus human adjudication (F1 score, % correctly classified end points) and replication of the EUCLID primary treatment effect
links.effect: Hybrid correctly classified 95.6% of end points vs 86.4% for ADAPT-CEC and 76.3% for GPT 4o; non-end points 99.6% vs 99.4% and 99.8%. Hybrid F1: CV death 0.94, MI 0.80, stroke 0.82, bleeding 0.83. ADAPT-CEC F1 was lower for CV death, MI and stroke. EUCLID primary HR 1.04 (95% CI 0.94-1.15) hybrid vs 1.02 (0.93-1.13) human.
links.tradeoff: Humans must still adjudicate the 30% of suspected events with the lowest AI prediction certainty, so some adjudication time and cost remain; no cost or time figures reported.
links.quote: A hybrid approach with humans adjudicating those suspected events with the lowest 30% of ADAPT-CEC prediction certainty was superior to ADAPT-CEC alone or GPT 4o alone and replicated the EUCLID primary outcome treatment effect.
